text:
Article Maker boosts traffic without spending

Artemiy Miller dropped this bombshell on Telegram, revealing that his creation has been quietly generating over 10,000 visitors per month without spending a single ruble on traffic. How did he manage to pull off such impressive numbers?
The Magic Behind "Статейник"

Artemiy’s “Статейник” is built for Claude Code and operates through 16 sub-agents that handle every aspect of content creation, from writing articles to adding images and publishing them on your website. Once you set up a task in simple language, the AI takes over and does everything else.

Imagine this: You provide instructions like "write an article about the benefits of meditation" or "create a blog post on the latest tech trends." The tool then generates high-quality content, adds images, and publishes it directly to your site. It even reviews its own strategy weekly based on traffic data from Yandex and Google.
The Numbers Speak

According to Artemiy’s claims, “Статейник” has produced more than 100 articles per month, attracting around 10,000 visitors from Yandex and Google without any paid traffic. That's not all—about a third of the revenue comes directly from search traffic.

One participant in Artemiy’s training program for ritual services managed to build their site in just eight hours using “Статейник.” In three weeks, the AI generated around 1,450 articles and brought in nearly 10,000 visitors from search engines. That's an average of over a thousand visits per day.
Cost Savings

The real kicker is that this participant didn’t need to hire an SEO specialist costing 70,000 rubles a month or pay for individual article writing at 500 rubles each. According to their calculations, they saved around one million rubles.

This kind of efficiency and cost reduction can be game-changing for businesses looking to scale up quickly without breaking the bank on content creation and SEO services.
How It Works

Setting up “Статейник” is straightforward: you provide instructions and prompts in Russian for all 16 stages of the process, and the AI takes care of everything else. However, you need a website where the articles can be published, and you have to subscribe to Claude or Codex.

The tool’s dashboard allows users to set up tasks, monitor progress, and adjust parameters as needed. You can also manage the publication of generated content on your own websites, ensuring full control over your digital presence.
What Is Stored

When you use “Статейник,” your input includes instructions and prompts in Russian for all 16 stages of content creation. The tool stores these inputs along with any generated content on its servers. It also tracks the performance metrics of each article, such as traffic and engagement data from Yandex and Google.

This tracking helps users understand which types of articles are performing well and adjust their strategies accordingly. However, it’s important to note that this data is used solely for improving the AI's performance and does not include any personal information beyond what is necessary for content generation.
What Is Excluded

The system does not store personal information beyond what is necessary to generate and publish articles. No user-specific data like email addresses or phone numbers are retained unless explicitly provided by the user for administrative purposes.

This ensures that users’ privacy remains intact while still benefiting from the AI’s powerful content creation capabilities.
User Controls

Users have control over their content generation process through a dashboard where they can set up tasks, monitor progress, and adjust parameters as needed. They also retain full ownership of any generated content and can manage its publication on their own websites.

This level of user control is crucial for ensuring that the AI-generated content aligns with your brand’s voice and messaging. You’re not just outsourcing your content creation; you’re actively guiding the process to meet your specific needs.
Availability

“Статейник” is currently available exclusively to users who subscribe to Claude or Codex platforms. The tool operates in Russian, which may limit accessibility for non-Russian speakers. However, the company behind it plans to expand language support in future updates.

This means that while “Статейник” offers significant benefits for those who can use it now, there’s potential for broader adoption as more languages are supported.
What This Does Not Prove

While Artemiy’s claims are impressive, they come with caveats. His results might not be replicable across different niches or industries due to varying market conditions and competition levels. Additionally, the effectiveness of “Статейник” depends heavily on the quality of prompts provided by users.

For example, if you’re in a highly competitive niche like tech gadgets, simply generating content may not be enough to attract significant traffic without additional SEO efforts. The AI’s success is also contingent on how well it understands and executes your specific instructions.
Practical Takeaway

Are you ready to embrace AI-driven content generation or stick with traditional methods? The real question is: why are we surprised when tech gets smarter and cheaper?

As technology advances, tools like “Статейник” offer new opportunities for businesses to streamline their operations and reduce costs. However, it’s important to approach these advancements with a critical eye and understand the limitations.

Let's talk about your thoughts in the comments. What’s your take on this new wave of automated content creation? Are you excited about the potential cost savings or skeptical about its effectiveness?

So, guys, are you ready to jump into the AI-driven content generation game? Or will you stick with tried-and-true methods for now? Share your thoughts and experiences in the comments below.

text:
Yesterday, live, I rebuilt @stripe's website. Pixel by pixel. Then I made it my own.

🔗 See it live: https://t.co/M1KTYguxVr

Why Stripe?
Because almost everything on it is built in code, where a simple image would have done the job. That's exactly what separates a generated website from a desired one.

Today, AI generates a landing page in 10 seconds.
The result: a purple gradient, 3 cards, a "Get started" button.
Everyone ends up with the same site. Nobody remembers it.

That was the heart of my Design Engineering training: 2 days to go from generated to desired.

Day 1: See, understand, direct
→ A Design Engineer ships end to end: design, code, optimize, improve
→ Taste lives in milliseconds: 1,000 ms linear feels tiring, 200 ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) feels natural
→ Train your eye: look at 10–30 sites a day, recreate them 1:1, publish
→ The invisible details: spacing scale, type hierarchy, every state, accessibility

Then the most important skill: directing AI with a real brief.

A generic prompt:
"Make me a modern landing page for a money transfer app."

A real brief has 6 ingredients:
1. Ambiance: 3 adjectives for the emotion you want (warm, confident, modern African)
2. Palette: one dominant color, one support, one accent (deep green + sun yellow on cream)
3. Typography: name the fonts and their role (editorial serif for headlines)
4. References: 1 to 3 sites to imitate in spirit (https://t.co/uAptF1lCNa for clarity)
5. Motion: durations, curves, what moves and why (200 ms ease-out entrances, nothing gratuitous)
6. Constraints: what's forbidden, accessibility, performance (no purple gradients, no emojis, no stock photos)

Same AI. Completely different result.

Day 2: Animate, polish, ship
→ Animate with intention: 150–300 ms, ease-out, transform and opacity only
→ Motion for everyday UI, GSAP for storytelling
→ The toolbox: shadcn/ui, TweakCN, Motion Primitives, Tabler Icons, React Scan
→ A beautiful slow site is still a bad site: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1

The Stripe case brought it all together: read the design, write the brief, rebuild it in code, animate it, then give it our own identity.

The lesson: AI doesn't replace taste. It amplifies it, if you know how to direct it.

text:
I have a lot of respect for Cedric and what he’s built, but I’d have to disagree with pretty much everything here.

“So you’re not really quitting, are you?”

By that logic, the Outdoor Boys haven’t quit YouTube either because their old videos are still up and generating revenue. Leaving your existing templates up doesn’t mean you haven’t quit. It just means that you’re leaving an existing asset to generate whatever revenue it still can, which is something I’d imagine most people would do.

“These creators never built distribution. They rented it from Framer.”

Uhm, yeah that’s how a marketplace works. The marketplace provides discovery, and creators provide the product. That’s not necessarily renting distribution any more than a YouTuber is renting an audience from YouTube. Templates are inherently discovery-driven products. People go to Framer because they need a website, and then they browse the marketplace, find something they like and move on.

You can build a personal brand around templates, and having an audience is obviously valuable, but templates dont naturally lend themselves to building a distribution channel in the same a newsletter, SaaS, or content business does. There’s also the difference between having an audience and having high-intent distribution. That’s why I dont think an owned distribution can replace marketplace distribution.

And that’s not unique to Framer either. The same thing happened to Notion templates, Webflow templates, UI kits, coding boilerplates, and other marketplace-driven products.

Yeah creators can diversify, build an audience, etc. but marketplace was part of the business model, and when that changes, the economics change with it.

quoted_tweet.text:
Template creators are rage-quitting Framer because Marketplace 3.0 tanked their sales.

Posting tearful goodbyes on X. Blaming the algorithm. Calling it quits.

But here's the kicker: they're leaving their templates up to keep collecting affiliate checks.

So you're not really quitting, are you?

Look, I get it. Sales dropped 70-80% overnight. That hurts.

But let's be real about what happened here.

These creators never built distribution. They rented it from Framer.

Marketplace 2.0 gave them free traffic. They made good templates. Some pulled multiple six figures. Amazing!

But the second the free tap turned off? Panic.

I was there in 2021-2022. Early beta. Built templates. Made multiple six figures doing it.

The difference? I built a personal brand. A newsletter. Grew my following. Every launch hit my own list of thousands, not just the marketplace feed.

Marketplace sales were always a bonus. Never the foundation.

That's why when I started Trueform, I knew exactly how to play the game. Same tactics. Different business. Built it to over a million.

Because I understood distribution from day one.

Now here's what's funny.

Marketplace 3.0 + Framer Skills + AI is about to unlock a whole new category of templates.

The opportunity is bigger than ever.

But everyone's leaving right when it's getting hard and interesting.

AI can help anyone build anything now. Tools are democratized.

What you can't build overnight? Real distribution.

That's always been the difference between renting an audience and owning one.

So if you're building in the Framer ecosystem: build your own channels. Your newsletter. Your following. Your voice.

Because platforms change. Algorithms shift. Marketplaces evolve.

But distribution you own?

That's yours forever.

text:
It’s likely that every business will have agents that interact with a consumer’s personal agent. The business won’t need a website, or a phone line, or an app, just an entry point on an app like Muse.

Purchases, appointment bookings, lead gen will happen via Muse and primarily in a conversational interface (unless visuals are a critical part of the specific commerce use case). Right now initiated by the consumer but obvious there will be a mechanism for a business to reach out directly to your personal agent.

This could change local commerce advertising, for example, if a business can bid on customers who aren’t just keyword searching but who express complex preferences that match more closely to a business’s offerings.

text:
RT @earcos: He tardado cuatro horas en hacer una factura en la app oficial de Facturae, lograr firmarla con mi certificado digital y conseguir subirla a la web de facturación de una de las top 5 agencias de medios más grandes del mundo, quee fundó hace más de 100 años.

Facturae está hecha en Java, la compraron a un dealer de software que tiene una máquina del tiempo y se la encargó a un developer que vive en 1994. 

La web de facturación de la agencia de medios fueron al mismo dealer de software, que esta vez fue a la época del punto com. En plena ebullición de los portales. Ahí encontró a un desarrollador y le diseño la web para enviar facturas.

He llorado de la frustración. Me he sentido en una película distópica y por momentos me he preguntado si en realidad estoy muerto y estoy en algún tipo de infierno donde me están torturando.

No puedo creer, ni imaginar, ni entender, ni concebir que, a punto de entrar a 2027, en un presente que ya hay coches que se conducen solos, las épocas de la IA, los robots y smartphones en el bolsillo que hacen vídeo con el que se han grabado películas, tengamos que, los contribuyentes, tener que afrontar este nivel de incompetencia. 

Es, posiblemente, el mayor y más horripilante ejemplo de la mierdificación de una gestión que he tenido que hacer como contribuyente en España.

Facturae está hecha en Java, la compraron a un dealer de software que tiene una máquina del tiempo y se la encargó a un developer que vive en 1994. 

La web de facturación de la agencia de medios fueron al mismo dealer de software, que esta vez fue a la época del punto com. En plena ebullición de los portales. Ahí encontró a un desarrollador y le diseño la web para enviar facturas.

He llorado de la frustración. Me he sentido en una película distópica y por momentos me he preguntado si en realidad estoy muerto y estoy en algún tipo de infierno donde me están torturando.

No puedo creer, ni imaginar, ni entender, ni concebir que, a punto de entrar a 2027, en un presente que ya hay coches que se conducen solos, las épocas de la IA, los robots y smartphones en el bolsillo que hacen vídeo con el que se han grabado películas, tengamos que, los contribuyentes, tener que afrontar este nivel de incompetencia. 

Es, posiblemente, el mayor y más horripilante ejemplo de la mierdificación de una gestión que he tenido que hacer como contribuyente en España.

Kissht business sounds similar to recently listed Moneyview.

While Onemi is built heavily around merchant ecosystems, originating as a point-of-sale (PoS) and checkout-finance platform that integrates directly with both physical retail counters and online checkout.

text:
RT @yhubee001: Felicia stared at the photo for a long moment. Then she closed the app.
Not because it no longer hurt.
But because healing had taught her something important. The harsh truth about life isn't that strangers can hurt you. It's that the people you trust most sometimes will. 

The engagement photo appeared online at 6:14 a.m.

By 6:15, Felicia had dropped her phone.

By 6:16, she was struggling to breathe.

And by 6:17, one question was tearing through her mind:

How do two people betray you without you noticing?

What Felicia didn't know was that the answer had started months earlier, long before the ring, long before the breakup, and long before the photo that would shatter her world.

---

Three months earlier.

Most betrayals don't begin with a kiss.

They begin with trust.

The kind of trust that makes you lower your guard around people you love.

The kind of trust that convinces you some people would never hurt you.

For Felicia, that person was Sophia.

They had been best friends since they were teenagers.

Sophia knew every embarrassing story, every failed relationship, every family secret, every dream Felicia was too afraid to tell anyone else.

When Felicia met Jones, Sophia was the first person she called.

When Jones asked her to move in with him, Sophia was the first person she told.

And when things started falling apart, Sophia became the person she leaned on the most.

That Friday evening, the three of them were having dinner together.

Nothing unusual.

Nothing dramatic.

At least that's how it looked.

Jones sat across from Felicia, occasionally checking his phone.

Sophia sat beside her, laughing at a story from work.

To anyone watching, they looked like people who genuinely enjoyed each other's company.

But beneath the surface, small things were changing.

The kind of things nobody notices until it's too late.

"You're quiet tonight," Felicia said to Jones.

Jones looked up.

"Hmm?"

"See?"

Felicia laughed.

"You weren't even listening."

"Sorry."

"Tough day?"

"Something like that."

Sophia took a sip of water.

Neither of them noticed Jones briefly glance in her direction.

Or maybe they did.

Maybe some part of Felicia noticed.

The problem with intuition is that it rarely arrives with proof.

Only discomfort.

The conversation continued.

Work.

Movies.

Travel plans.

Normal topics.

Yet every now and then Felicia felt like she had walked into a room after everyone else had already finished talking.

A strange feeling she couldn't explain.

As dinner ended, Jones stood.

"I'll grab dessert."

The moment he disappeared toward the counter, Sophia's phone lit up on the table.

Just for a second.

A notification flashed.

Sophia quickly turned the screen over.

Too quickly.

Felicia frowned.

"Everything okay?"

Sophia smiled.

"Yeah."

Something about the answer felt rehearsed.

Not suspicious.

Just... fast.

Like someone closing a door before you realize it was open.

Felicia ignored the feeling.

That's what people do when they trust someone.

---

A week later, Felicia found herself sitting across from Sophia in their favorite café.

Outside, people hurried through the rain.

Inside, the smell of coffee filled the air.

Sophia immediately noticed something was wrong.

"You look exhausted."

Felicia rubbed her forehead.

"I barely slept."

"Why?"

Felicia hesitated.

Because saying something out loud makes it feel more real.

"Do you ever feel like you're losing someone while they're still standing right in front of you?"

Sophia's expression changed.

Only slightly.

But enough.

"What happened?"

"It's Jones."

Sophia looked down at her coffee.

"Did you two argue?"

"No."

"Then what?"

Felicia sighed.

"That's the problem."

Sophia waited.

"We don't argue anymore."

"What does that mean?"

"It means he stopped trying."

The words hung between them.

Felicia stared through the café window.

"Have you ever watched someone slowly check out of a relationship?"

Sophia remained silent.

The engagement photo appeared online at 6:14 a.m.

By 6:15, Felicia had dropped her phone.

By 6:16, she was struggling to breathe.

And by 6:17, one question was tearing through her mind:

How do two people betray you without you noticing?

What Felicia didn't know was that the answer had started months earlier, long before the ring, long before the breakup, and long before the photo that would shatter her world.

---

Three months earlier.

Most betrayals don't begin with a kiss.

They begin with trust.

The kind of trust that makes you lower your guard around people you love.

The kind of trust that convinces you some people would never hurt you.

For Felicia, that person was Sophia.

They had been best friends since they were teenagers.

Sophia knew every embarrassing story, every failed relationship, every family secret, every dream Felicia was too afraid to tell anyone else.

When Felicia met Jones, Sophia was the first person she called.

When Jones asked her to move in with him, Sophia was the first person she told.

And when things started falling apart, Sophia became the person she leaned on the most.

That Friday evening, the three of them were having dinner together.

Nothing unusual.

Nothing dramatic.

At least that's how it looked.

Jones sat across from Felicia, occasionally checking his phone.

Sophia sat beside her, laughing at a story from work.

To anyone watching, they looked like people who genuinely enjoyed each other's company.

But beneath the surface, small things were changing.

The kind of things nobody notices until it's too late.

"You're quiet tonight," Felicia said to Jones.

Jones looked up.

"Hmm?"

"See?"

Felicia laughed.

"Sorry."

"Tough day?"

"Something like that."

Sophia took a sip of water.

Or maybe they did.

Maybe some part of Felicia noticed.

The problem with intuition is that it rarely arrives with proof.

Only discomfort.

The conversation continued.

Work.

Movies.

Travel plans.

Normal topics.

Yet every now and then Felicia felt like she had walked into a room after everyone else had already finished talking.

A strange feeling she couldn't explain.

As dinner ended, Jones stood.

"I'll grab dessert."

The moment he disappeared toward the counter, Sophia's phone lit up on the table.

Just for a second.

Too quickly.

Sophia smiled.

"Yeah."

Something about the answer felt rehearsed.

Not suspicious.

Just... fast.

Like someone closing a door before you realize it was open.

Felicia ignored the feeling.

That's what people do when they trust someone.

Global markets, factories and energy

China: Tesla rolled out new incentives for orders placed by Oct 31, with 5,000 yuan off any Model 3, 7,000 yuan off select Model Y trims and up to five years of 0% financing, per CnEVPost. Tesla also launched an improved Model 3 in China with vehicle to load, a larger cabin screen and new interior options, per Teslarati. Tesla's recall of about 2.98 million imported and China made Model 3, Y, S and X vehicles over emergency door releases began Sep 25, with warning labels and an over the air update, per Reuters. Musk called Giga Shanghai a gem in a China Media Group interview.

Europe: ACEA data showed Tesla EU registrations up 52.7% year over year in August and 65.9% year to date. Giga Berlin is pushing toward 7,500 cars a week by mid October, and Tesla's 4% to 5% wage raise there took effect Oct 1, with a new performance bonus for skilled staff, per Handelsblatt.

4/6
Software, FSD and AI

FSD (Supervised) v14.3.10 is rolling out to HW4 cars in North America inside update 2026.27.11. It follows v14.3.9, which falsely told many owners to clean their front cameras. Tesla confirmed the bug, is canceling service visits booked because of it, and owners who already paid for a cleaning can ask Tesla Support for a refund, per Electrek and Not a Tesla App. HW3 Model S and Model X cars began receiving FSD v14.2 Lite for the first time, and HW3 Model 3 and Y also get arrival options, parking and reversing in the Lite build. The same update adds Automatic Collision Evasion on HW4 and Vehicle to Home with Powerwall, so a parked, plugged in Tesla can share battery with a Powerwall during an outage via Charging then Powershare.

Grok is getting more useful in the car. Tesla added Grok Connectors for email, calendar and files, plus Grok Bot for hands free errands like ordering coffee, shopping or booking appointments. Grok Bot currently requires a SuperGrok Heavy subscription. Separately, Tesla's Q2 2026 active FSD paid subscription base stood at 1.48 million, up from 0.95 million in Q2 2025, a scale check that will refresh with Q3 earnings on Oct 21.

In Europe, FSD approval slipped again. The agenda for the EU's Oct 6 TCMV meeting lists only a continuation of discussions on the Dutch application, so an EU wide vote cannot come before December, per Electrek. Separately, a Brussels test by the Belgian road safety nonprofit Johanna found FSD exceeded the limit in 55% of tested 30 km/h zones, averaging 44 km/h.

Optimus: according to The Information, Fremont is now building several hundred robots a week, about ten times the Q2 pace, and targets over 1,000 a week by year end. The hands, which need more than 100 hand assembled parts, and the AI's ability to generalize remain the bottlenecks, per Electrek and Ars Technica. Reporting this week also said Tesla cut AI5 and AI6 chip memory to secure Optimus volume. The new $30 billion credit package is explicitly framed around scaling Cybercab, Optimus and Semi capacity.

Sources: Electrek, Not a Tesla App, TeslaNorth, Ars Technica, TechCrunch, Tesla IR.

text:
3/6
Roadster, Robotaxi and Cybercab

Roadster: the invite only outdoor reveal is Thursday Oct 15 in Waco, Texas, near SpaceX McGregor, after Tesla rescheduled from Oct 1 for severe weather. Electrive and Tesla Oracle both refreshed the slip as the original date passed. Specs, price and production timing remain unconfirmed, with earlier guidance still pointing to 2027 or 2028 for production. Tesla closed the Semi event with a short teaser showing a thin full width light bar plus Tesla and SpaceX logos.

On autonomy, Texas registrations reached 546 robotaxi vehicles as of late September, 420 Model Y and 126 Cybercab, per Tesla Oracle and EVwire citing state data. The Robotaxi app also notified riders that the Cybercab fleet had doubled, with Teslarati putting active Cybercab availability near 125 units in Austin. Registered is not the same as active: a community tracker counted only 8 vehicles carrying riders in Austin in the 7 days to Sep 22, per Electrek. Tesla also says it now builds a Cybercab drive unit every 10 seconds. Musk told China Media Group that Cybercab is operating commercially in Texas, will soon run in Florida and Nevada and other states, and should be commercial in California by the middle of next year.

The NHTSA clock hit Wednesday Sep 30: Tesla was required to answer Special Order AQ26002 under oath, explaining how Cybercab meets federal safety standards without a steering wheel, pedals or mirrors. The Audit Query covers roughly 1,000 vehicles and does not by itself order a stop sale or service halt. As of Saturday Oct 3, three days after the deadline, no public confirmation of a filing was available.

Sources: TechCrunch, Electrek, Electrive, Teslarati, Tesla Oracle, EVwire, NHTSA.

text:
1/6
Tesla Weekly Review
Covering the last 7 days, Sep 27 to Oct 3

What is new since yesterday: Tesla printed official Q3 2026 results on Friday Oct 2. Deliveries were 486,532 and production was 464,391, with Model 3 and Model Y at 478,237 delivered and 457,387 produced, and other models at 8,295 delivered and 7,004 produced. Energy storage deployed 13.7 GWh. That delivery total beat Tesla's own company compiled mean of 461,974 and the median of 463,406 by roughly 25,000 units, and it beat every named estimate on that sheet. Storage came in below the 15.9 GWh street expectation and below the 14.2 GWh record from Q4 2025, while still up from 13.5 GWh in Q2 and 12.5 GWh a year earlier. TSLA closed Friday at $370.59, up $16.48 or 4.65% from Thursday's $354.11 close after the beat.

The week also locked in the financing and autonomy backdrop that framed the print. On Tuesday Sep 29 Tesla lined up $30 billion in fresh undrawn senior unsecured credit, a $20 billion three year delayed draw term loan with Citibank as agent, plus an $8 billion five year revolver and a $2 billion 364 day revolver with Wells Fargo as agent. It replaces a prior $5 billion revolver. Tesla said it has no borrowings outstanding and does not currently plan to draw in 2026, while still guiding more than $25 billion of 2026 capital spending for Cybercab, Optimus, Semi and related buildout. Late September Texas registrations reached 546 robotaxi vehicles, 420 Model Y and 126 Cybercab, and the Robotaxi app told riders the Cybercab fleet had doubled. NHTSA's sworn Cybercab Special Order answers were due Wednesday Sep 30; three days later neither Tesla nor NHTSA has publicly confirmed a filing.

Sources: Tesla 8 K, CNBC, Electrek, TechCrunch, Reuters, Teslarati.

RT @davepl1968: Last week, I had Astra produce a boot disc image featuring a custom graphics demo app for the PDP-11 running on the 1977 Terak 8510 computer.

Astra thought hard and produced an IMD file, which I wrote to an 8" floppy using a Greaseweazle and the drives out of my IMSAI.

It booted and ran the first try.  So it went one better than just producing assembly language!  It produced an executable binary AND a boot loader.  For a computer that is NOT especially well documented, either.

Each week I feel like AI is as smart as its ever going to be, then six months later, I can't believe how stupid it used to be!

Model Y L gear

The Tesla Model Y L Roof Rack is made for the six seat Model Y L only. Aluminum crossbars with T slots and locking towers mount with no drilling and are rated to 165 lbs.

It lists at $500 on the Tesla Shop. It landed with the US Model Y L accessory launch on Sep 16 to 17 as first deliveries begin.

Review highlight: mount points shift on the longer roof, so a standard Model Y rack will not line up. Tesla pitches this rack for low wind noise.

Owner comments: no owner reviews yet, because Model Y L deliveries are only starting.

Tesla offers a Model Y L Air Mattress and side window privacy curtains sized for the longer Model Y L cabin. Both already sell in China.

US price is coming soon. They were left out of the US launch and Tesla still has not posted a US price or date.

Review highlight: launch coverage called these the biggest miss for anyone hoping to camp in a Model Y L.

Comments: one aftermarket seller has not cleared a Model Y L fit for its own mattresses or shades either, so wait before buying a regular Model Y set.

Sources: Not a Tesla App, EV Bandit.

text:
2/6
Cybertruck bed gear

The Tesla Cybertruck Bed Gear Box clips onto every Cybertruck trim. Its lockable aluminum shell sits on the bed L track at roughly 56 by 20 by 8 inches and includes two organizer bins. Long Range and Dual Motor AWD need the L Tracks accessory installed first.

It lists at $985 on the Tesla Shop, launched Sep 3.

Review highlight: writers call it a premium buy and note the empty weight near 57 lbs, which trims payload before tools or recovery gear go in.

Owner comments: fans praise the factory look, some wish for more height under the tonneau, and others ask whether MOLLE panels must come off. One owner reports the spare tire kit still clears.

The Tesla Cybertruck Tailgate Utility Track works on every Cybertruck trim. An aluminum bar bolts to the gate with a T slot channel, two L track points and two load stops so long cargo stays put on the folded gate.

It lists at $350 on the Tesla Shop, launched Sep 3.

Review highlight: Teslarati describes it as a worksite add on that turns the folded gate into another tie down surface for lumber or a cooler.

Owner comments: in the launch thread, owners asked Tesla for a simple bed step next, and one tip was using the bumper as a toe hold to climb in.

Sources: Not a Tesla App, Teslarati, Basenor, Cybertruck Owners Club.

text:
A lot of people are pointing out that the storage is only 32 GB
While it’s true that newer software takes up a lot of storage space
An older device cannot update to new software 
If you see this there could be couple of reasons causing it:
1. You offload apps and not delete them, each app takes up 2 distinct storage space on your device, the app size which is a known size when you downloaded it, and documents and data which is linked to your own usage.
When you offload an app or delete it from your homes screen, you only delete the app itself while keeping the document and data which may actually take up a much larger space on your storage.
In older softwares, you will need to go to your device’s storage and delete it from there.
I can see 3GB in your offloaded streaming services already. 

2. You may have a bug that locally happened on your device, so deleting apps wouldn’t help as your device will keep recognizing that storage as being used by your system
Which in this case you need to make sure that all apps that you need are synced to iCloud (not backed up, as the back up will bring that bug back)
Then you can restore your device using a computer
And set it up as new… not from a backup
Once you log in to your Apple ID AFTER selecting “do not transfer any data”, your native Apple apps should start syncing
And then you can download the apps from the App Store.

I hope this helps.

2. You may have a bug that locally happened on your device, so deleting apps wouldn’t help as your device will keep recognizing that storage as being used by your system
Which in this case you need to make sure that all apps that you need are synced to iCloud (not backed up, as the back up will bring that bug back)
Then you can restore your device using a computer
And set it up as new… not from a backup
Once you log in to your Apple ID AFTER selecting “do not transfer any data”, your native Apple apps should start syncing
And then you can download the apps from the App Store.

I hope this helps.

text:
Multi-outcome markets create an easy engineering trap:
each outcome has its own order book, but the positions aren’t independent.
If exactly one outcome must settle Yes, then the real state lives at the question level—not inside any single book.
A bot can reconcile every order correctly and still misunderstand its total exposure.
The safer model is:
question identity → linked inventories → conversion operations → conservation checks
Local correctness isn’t enough when the contracts share a global invariant.

text:
RT @gregisenberg: THE VIBE MANUFACTURING PLAYBOOK

1. Measure everything. Digital calipers for small parts, a phone LiDAR app like Polycam to scan a space or an object. Bad measurements are the #1 reason first builds fail

2. Have a frontier model write the design as code. Describe the part to a model like Claude Opus 5.5 or Astra, and have it write the design in a codebased CAD tool like OpenSCAD or CadQuery. Zoo's Text to CAD does it in one step!

3. Use real CAD files. The text to 3D models on Hugging Face make shapes that look right, but factories need precise files: STEP for machined parts, DXF for lasercut metal, STL for 3D printing

4. Make sure it can be made. Ask the AI to check the design against how factories actually work: how tight metal can bend, how small a hole can be, how much wiggle room parts need etc...

5. Prototype in plastic first. A $300 to $600 home 3D printer like a Bambu Lab lets you test the fit overnight before paying for metal (really fun to play with too!)

6. Pay an engineer for 1 hour. Before your first real order, have a mechanical engineer on Upwork etc review the files. It's the cheapest insurance you'll ever buy.

7. Send it out. SendCutSend cuts and bends metal, Xometry and Protolabs handle machining and plastic, JLCPCB builds circuit boards. Instant quotes, and parts usually ship in days.

8. Add the brains. Most smart features run on a cheap wifi chip like the ESP32. Design the board in KiCad, and use ESPHome to control it straight from your phone.

9. Make one, then fix it. Your first version will be off somewhere! Order a single unit, test it, and adjust.

10. Do the math. Add up parts, finishing, assembly, packaging, and shipping. Custom products are hard to resell, so price for healthy margins.

11. Sell the design and make to order. Let customers adjust the measurements, and only manufacture after they pay. Zero warehouse, zero unsold stock.

12. Handle the boring part. If it plugs into a wall or touches kids, you'll need safety certification. It's slow and annoying, which is exactly why it's a moat.

13. Scale when it works. Once orders are steady, switch to batch runs and your cost per unit drops fast.

Vibe coding changed who can build software!

Vibe manufacturing is about to change who can build things!!

Even if you just want to make things for yourself (and not make things for others)

WELCOME TO THE VIBE MANUFACTURING ERA

text:
𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗔 𝗖𝗟𝗜𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗚𝗘𝗧𝗦 𝗜𝗧𝗦 𝗣𝗘𝗘𝗥 𝗜𝗗

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer has written a new BitTorrent client. It can speak the protocol, talk to trackers and exchange pieces. Now it has to introduce itself, because every tracker request and every peer handshake carries a 20 byte field called the peer id.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The peer id has to do more than distinguish one peer from another. BEP 20 explains that it has traditionally been used to identify the client implementation and its version as well. Without a shared convention, every client invents its own scheme, and everyone else is left guessing. The proposal even keeps a list of clients that have been seen in the wild and still need to be identified, with codes BD, NP and wF as examples. An unlabeled client is a puzzle for tracker operators and for other developers trying to understand what they are talking to.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

That is the gap BEP 20, Peer ID Conventions, fills. It is an Active Process BEP by David Harrison, created Feb 27, 2008, and it records the established conventions in one place, derived originally from community work.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer picks a style. The mainline client begins its peer id with M followed by the version number written in ASCII digits with major, minor and tiny parts separated by marks, so version 4.3.6 and version 4.20.8 are both representable. Many clients use another style: a short marker, then a two character client code, four ASCII digits for the version, and a closing marker, with the remaining bytes random. Other families, such as the style of Shad0w's client and BitTornado, use a single letter and up to five characters of version. The developer registers nothing; they follow the convention and expect others to recognize it.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The finished client now announces itself clearly. The list in the BEP shows how many families have used the idea: UT stands for µTorrent, UW for µTorrent Web, qB for qBittorrent, TR for Transmission, DE for DelugeTorrent, lt for libTorrent and WW for WebTorrent, among dozens more.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

For the person using the client, none of this is visible, and that is the goal. Their client joins swarms, tracker operators can tell which software they are serving, and other developers can reason about behavior across implementations. A bug that affects one version can be traced to that version.

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡: The BTT design points out that the open protocol has been used to create dozens of independent clients with healthy competition, while BitTorrent Inc.'s own clients account for an estimated 40% of protocol activity. Any economy layered on top has to work across all of them, and a shared way of saying who is who is part of making that possible. When BTT bids travel through swarms as protocol extensions, they travel among clients that already know how to identify one another.

A small convention in a 20 byte field helps a large ecosystem stay legible, and BitTorrent on TRON will keep depending on this kind of shared understanding as more developers build.

@justinsuntron @BitTorrent #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗫 𝗖𝗟𝗜𝗘𝗡𝗧

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to work in the Codex client every day and wants to choose the best model for each task without leaving it. Some tasks need a flagship, some need speed, and some need a model from a different vendor entirely.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The obstacle is breadth. A client built around one vendor's models makes it awkward to use others, and every additional model family means another set of credentials and another round of configuration. The developer ends up using whichever models were easiest to wire up rather than whichever are best.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

https://t.co/QPRInngWC8's Responses API is the missing piece. It reached GPT and DeepSeek series first, was extended to GLM and Kimi on September 22 so that four major series were covered, and was upgraded on September 24 to be fully compatible with upstream standard protocols. After that, any model on the platform that supports the Responses API can be called uniformly through /v1/responses. The official API full set group added MiMo, Qwen and Hunyuan, while the Mix and OL Station optional service provider group added OpenAI, Gemini and Grok.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Integration takes only the minimal configuration of an API Key and a Base URL. After that, https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 says that when it adds new models from integrated vendors, developers will not need additional configuration to bring them into the Codex client.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

With the connection in place, the developer builds the way they prefer. Routine edits can go to a fast, low cost model, deep refactors to a flagship such as GPT 6.1 Sol with its multi agent delegation in Beta, and large codebase reviews to a model with a 1M token context such as Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Kimi K2.8 Preview. The application the developer ships is better because each part of the work used a fitting model.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

End users of that application feel the result as quality and speed, without knowing which models were involved. Their activity generates usage that flows back through the platform's settlement layer.

This developer story is the contribution https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 makes to TRON: infrastructure that turns an open choice of models into something a builder can use with a single configuration, and the next models added will appear in that client with no extra steps.

@justinsuntron @BAI_AGI #TRONEcoStar

𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗨𝗦𝗘 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗗

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants an AI agent that can do more than describe a stablecoin. They want it to open a Vault, check its health, swap through the PSM and deposit into savings, all from a conversation.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Reading data is easy. Writing to a chain is not. An agent that can sign transactions can also make costly mistakes, from guessing an address to approving more than intended or acting without the user's consent. A naive integration would leave all of that risk to chance.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

The missing piece is the official USDD MCP server. It lets agents interact with the protocol across TRON, Ethereum and BNB Chain, covering the full Vault lifecycle, PSM swaps, savings deposits and withdrawals, token transfers and protocol analytics, including treasury and Smart Allocator views. Safety is built in. Private keys are encrypted and stored locally and are never returned by any tool. Token transfers follow a two step flow in which a preview must be confirmed before execution, and a pending confirmation expires after 10 minutes. Every tool is classified by side effect, and hosts are expected to surface any write for user approval.

A companion skills package adds behavior rules. Its four skills cover Vaults, the PSM, Earn and analytics, and every write passes an eleven point gate: explicit network, address resolution from official sources, wallet and gas checks, balance and allowance checks, a clear confirmation summary and a fresh affirmative reply from the user.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer needs Node.js 20 or later, adds the server to the client configuration for Claude Desktop, Cursor or a project file for Claude Code, and optionally supplies a TronGrid key for more reliable TRON access. Wallets are handled either through a browser extension such as TronLink or an encrypted local agent wallet.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The result is an assistant that can answer practical questions and act on the answers. It can list available Vault types on a network, inspect a position, explain collateral buffers and prepare a transfer for approval.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

A user asks whether they are close to liquidation on a particular Vault. The agent reads the Vault summary, runs a risk analysis and explains the health factor and collateral buffer. If the risk is critical, the skill refuses to mint more or withdraw collateral and recommends repaying or topping up instead. If the user says to skip the checks, the checks still run.

The contribution to TRON is a template for responsible automation. As agents start handling money, an ecosystem needs stablecoins that come with guardrails as well as endpoints, and USDD's MCP server and skills show how TRON can welcome software users without giving up user control.

@justinsuntron @USDDecentralize #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗥𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗟 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗧𝗢 𝗔𝗜

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer on TRON wants to build an application where an AI model reacts to the world as it is right now. The official WINkLink account asked the question in September 2025: why settle for static data when AI can make it smarter? Its answer was to deliver timely and reliable real world data to AI models through WINkLink on TRON.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer hits a wall quickly. A smart contract cannot call an API, so it cannot ask the world anything on its own. An AI model can read data, but if that data is stale or comes from a single unverified source, the model's decisions are only as good as its worst input. The developer needs a channel that is timely, reliable and checkable on chain.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

WINkLink's AnyAPI service is the missing piece. It lets developers obtain data from any off chain source, transform it and feed it back to the chain, and it is backed by a node network that handles the retrieval. A long list of internal adapters covers the transformations: HTTP calls, JSON parsing, encoding and decoding, string handling, comparisons, and arithmetic such as multiply, divide, sum, mean and median.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer writes a consumer contract, either a single word version that returns one value or a multi word version that returns several, and points it at the operator contract. They set the job identifier, fund the contract with WIN and test on the Nile testnet, where sample operator contracts and jobs are available for learning. The guidance is firm that samples are for practice and that real applications should use their own consumer contracts and carefully designed job specifications.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The finished application takes a live fact, such as a rate, a status or a measurement, and brings it on chain through AnyAPI. A smart contract can then store it, act on it or expose it to the AI component that sits beside it. Where the application also needs prices, it can read WINkLink price feeds, and where it needs fair selection, it can use verifiable randomness.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

Users never see the oracle. They see an application that responds to current conditions, whether that is adjusting an outcome, settling a claim or triggering an action. Each of those interactions sends a small payment in WIN to the node network that did the retrieval, which feeds activity back into the ecosystem.

That cycle is the contribution WINkLink makes to TRON. A developer with an idea does not have to build a data pipeline, negotiate with providers or invent a trust model. They write the application logic, and the infrastructure for real world input already exists, paid for in a token the chain already uses.

As builders pair AI with on chain logic, WINkLink is positioned to supply the live data that makes those applications worth using.

@justinsuntron @WinkLink_Oracle #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗢𝗡 𝗝𝗨𝗦𝗧𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗗 𝗩𝟮

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to build a portfolio tracker for TRON users. It should show how much a person has deposited into JustLend V2 vaults and how healthy their positions are. The first move is the obvious one: look for a public data API.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Here the developer meets a limit that the JustLend V2 reference states openly. The public gateway currently serves V1 only, and V2 protocol data is not yet published there. The reference adds that V2 endpoints will be added to the OpenAPI specification once they are live on the public gateway and their paths are verified. A tracker that depends on a REST endpoint for V2 would have to wait.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

The reference points to two ways forward: the JustLend MCP server, whose get_moolah tools return read only V2 data, or reading the contracts directly on chain. The infrastructure behind both is the V2 contract set on TRON mainnet. It includes MoolahProxy for core lending, a TrxProviderProxy that handles native TRX by wrapping and unwrapping WTRX, a PublicLiquidatorProxy, a ResilientOracle and an interest rate model, plus ERC4626 vaults for TRX, USDT and USDD.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer chooses the MCP route for data and uses the published ABIs for contract calls. Every V2 market is defined by a loan token, a collateral token, an oracle, an interest rate model and a liquidation loan to value, and a position's risk is reported as a ratio against that value, where anything above 1.0 means the position can be liquidated. That one number is exactly what a health indicator needs.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The result is a tracker that lists vault shares and market positions, flags positions whose risk ratio approaches 1.0 and warns users in advance. The reference also cautions to always verify addresses against on chain data before integrating.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

A user opens the tracker and sees vault deposits and market positions in one place, then decides whether to add collateral, repay or withdraw. Each of those actions runs through the same contracts the tracker reads.

𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗘𝗔𝗡𝗦 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡

The sequence shows an infrastructure that is honest about its gaps and gives builders a clear way around them. For TRON, that openness invites more developers to build on lending, and each new tool that does so brings more users to the protocol.

@justinsuntron @DeFi_JUST #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗪𝗛𝗢 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗦 𝗢𝗡 𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗧

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer has an idea for a decentralized application. It will let people share data, keep important files somewhere durable and take part in the network around it. As a BitTorrent ecosystem post puts it, building decentralized applications requires more than innovative ideas, since it also depends on infrastructure that can reliably support data sharing, storage and network participation.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The limitation appears the moment the developer sketches the architecture. Storage that sits on a single centralized provider brings back the single point of failure the application was meant to avoid. Building a peer to peer network from nothing means solving discovery, incentives and reliability before writing a single feature. And an application that serves several blockchain communities needs to move value between them.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

This is where BitTorrent supplies the missing pieces. The post names three kinds of technology that form part of the foundation: peer to peer networking, decentralized storage through BTFS, and cross chain infrastructure through BitTorrent Chain. Together they form the base the developer needs without having to invent it.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Integration follows two clear routes. For data, the developer uses BTFS, where files are distributed across participating nodes, and expands storage beyond traditional centralized infrastructure. For connectivity, the developer uses BTTC, which supports interoperability between multiple blockchain ecosystems, runs an EVM compatible virtual machine and gives the application a chain with low fees and fast confirmation. In BTFS 4.0, file metadata is managed through smart contracts on BTTC, so even the record of what is stored can be checked on chain.

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔 𝗟𝗜𝗕𝗥𝗔𝗥𝗬 𝗗𝗔𝗣𝗣

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗
A developer wants to build a small application on TRON that feels like a real product: a library where items can be listed, rented and returned, with a wallet connected frontend that always shows the right state. This is Track 3 on the TRON Developer Hub, the path for DApp developers, and its goal is to connect a contract, a wallet and the frontend.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The hard part is not writing the contract. It is knowing what is true. A wallet signs a transaction, the frontend sends it, and a node replies that the broadcast call completed without error. The Hub is clear that this does not mean the transaction was included or executed successfully. The interface must not claim a book is rented because a broadcast returned true. The developer also needs a dependable way to keep the page in step with on chain events, and a way to prove that the code on chain is the code they wrote.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘
TRON supplies the missing pieces. TronLink serves as the wallet and signing entry point for DApps. TronGrid provides the API gateway and indexing for transaction history and contract events. TRONSCAN provides block explorer and data views for checking results. The confirmation semantics guide gives the rules for reading receipts and solidified state, and the Hub's contract tooling covers testing and deployment.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The track's exercise is specific. The developer tests and deploys a library contract on the Shasta testnet, then wires up TronLink for listing, renting, confirmation and event synchronization. Completion is proven with evidence: the test result, the Shasta contract address, the deployment and call transaction IDs, source verification and negative cases, the failure paths where something is supposed to be rejected. The shared constraints add a safeguard: private keys, seed phrases and API keys never go into source, logs or screenshots.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The result is a working library DApp. A librarian lists an item, and a reader connects TronLink to rent it. The application does not display success when the wallet signs. It waits for the transaction to be confirmed and for the contract's event to arrive, and only then updates the screen.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬
For a real user, all of this is invisible, which is exactly the goal. They connect a wallet, rent a book and see an accurate result. If a transaction fails, the page says so, because the developer practiced the negative cases in advance.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡
This sequence shows what TRON offers builders beyond a fast chain. The network gives developers an ordered path from test to deployment, tools that handle signing and indexing, and clear definitions of what confirmation means. That is how a network with more than 405 million accounts keeps attracting applications whose users can trust what the screen tells them.

As more developers follow tracks like this one, TRON's applications will keep getting more reliable for the people who use them.

@justinsuntron @trondao #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗦 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗦 𝗢𝗡 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to build an application that uses AI. The vision is clear: a Web3 native product with intelligence built into it, running on TRON, where the official message tells builders to believe in TRON and build on TRON. What the application needs is dependable access to AI models, a way to identify users and a way to settle payments.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The need is easy to state and harder to meet. Developers need APIs, creators need usable interfaces, agents need tools and applications need reliable AI services, and those pieces rarely arrive in one place. Traditional AI services tend to ask for email registration, credit card details and separate subscriptions, none of which suit an application that works with wallets and onchain payments.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

This is where AINFT's infrastructure becomes the missing piece. Its ecosystem brings together AI chat, AI APIs, multiple models, Web3 authentication and TRON based payments. AI models provide intelligence, APIs provide developer access, the blockchain provides identity and settlement, and wallet infrastructure provides authentication. By abstracting access to TRON and BNB Chain, the architecture also lets AI agents query balances, execute transfers and call smart contracts without needing to understand RPC interfaces or gas mechanics.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Integration follows the same wallet centered logic. The user connects a wallet, which serves as their identity, and the application draws on pay as you go credits that can be funded with TRX, USDT, USDD or NFTs. The developer does not have to build separate accounts, billing and model connections, because they arrive through the same gateway that users reach with a single signature.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The finished application inherits those properties. It can offer several models to its users, accept TRON based payments and recognize people by their wallets. For the creator side of the ecosystem, it can also sit next to NFT Pump collections and AI powered creation, so that intelligence and ownership live in the same product.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

For the person using it, the experience is simple. They connect a wallet, ask a question or create something, and the credits move onchain. They never register an account, because the wallet was the account from the start.

The contribution to TRON is a lower barrier for builders. When identity, payment and model access are handled by shared infrastructure, a developer can spend time on the idea instead of the plumbing, and every application built this way adds another reason to use the network.

As more developers choose to build on that foundation, the phrase about TRON becoming the home of AI will increasingly describe a list of working applications.

@justinsuntron @AINFTcom #TRONEcoStar

text:
The people yearn for creativity.

They want to make things that feel like theirs, and trade things that feel like they found them. A launch that is not the same curve everyone else pressed this morning. Uniqueness is the product. Attention is the whole game, and creativity is what moves the trenches.

I have always wondered why nobody shipped the pad that simply lets the chain do what the chain can already do. Programmable. Modular. A catalog instead of a costume. The final boss of launching.

The pads we have set the terms for you. A basic pair. A tax. One or two launch styles a team decided were enough. If the thing you actually want is missing, you need a developer, or AI writing the code beside you, or you build another launchpad on top of the launchpad. That stack exists because the pad underneath is missing the feature, cannot ship it in time, or does not want to. So someone forks the factory, and the pile gets taller for no reason.

"Hooks" is the attempt to end that pile.

You do not need a developer anymore. You play with the Legos. You stack them. You launch. It is tradable. You did not write a program, and you did not wait on someone else. The chain enforces the rule. Whatever you stacked is the product.

One place where the creative act is assembly. Piece by piece. The more pieces that exist, the more launches that used to require a new entity become something you can ship the same day. Every one of those launches is an advertisement for the place that made it possible.

It is the same bet on both rails. On EVM, the liquidity already sits on Uniswap, and Uniswap v4 already runs on hooks. On Solana, the rule sits inside the token, and you compose it the same way with Token-2022. People have been building pads on top of pads because the hook was powerful and the menu in front of it was not. If the pad is the catalog, you do not need your own factory.

Be as creative as the pieces allow. People want uniqueness. Getting this close to an endgame launchpad is the chance you take.

The scarce thing was never ideas. It was making them real. The Legos are at the user's disposal now. The trenches will use whatever lets them ship the thing they could already see.

text:
𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗦 𝗢𝗡 𝗝𝗨𝗦𝗧𝗟𝗘𝗡𝗗 𝗗𝗔𝗢 𝗔𝗣𝗜𝗦

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer building a wallet, a portfolio dashboard or a liquidation monitor on TRON wants live lending data: market rates, account positions, staking state and energy rental orders. They want it structured, typed and reliable enough to put in front of users.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Reading everything directly from contracts is slow and repetitive, and history is harder still. The API returns current state, and there is no official hosted indexer for historical events such as Mint, Borrow, RepayBorrow or LiquidateBorrow. Anyone who wants a full history has to plan for it, whether by filtering events through TronGrid, which retains roughly 30 days, or by running their own indexer against an archive node.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

JustLend DAO fills the gap with a public HTTP API described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification, so it can be imported into Swagger, Postman or an LLM tool. Endpoints cover all markets, per address positions, sTRX and Energy Rental dashboards, V2 vaults, V2 markets and aggregated V2 portfolios, and even a list of accounts above the liquidation observation threshold. Contract addresses for Mainnet and Nile ship as machine readable files, and JSON ABI files carry the canonical event signatures.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer calls the markets endpoint for supply and borrow APY, TVL and prices, and the account endpoint for positions and health. Numbers arrive as strings, so a big decimal library keeps precision on large values. Errors come back inside the response body with an HTTP 200 status, so the code branches on the body's code field. For heavier reads, the MCP server batches account queries through Multicall3, cutting them from around 8 seconds to around 2.5.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The result is a dashboard that shows a wallet's supply, borrow and staking positions together, or a monitor that watches the high risk account list and alerts liquidators when positions cross the threshold. The same building blocks work for a wallet that wants to show yields before a user deposits.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

The end user sees rates, health and balances in an interface they already use, without knowing which endpoint served them. They supply, borrow, stake and rent Energy with current information, and liquidators find eligible positions faster, which keeps the lending pool healthy for everyone.

That is JustLend DAO's contribution to TRON's developer side: the protocol is not only usable through its own app but reachable through published, typed and candid interfaces that state their own limits. Each new application built on those interfaces extends the protocol's reach, and the developers still to arrive will find the same clear starting point.

@justinsuntron @DeFi_JUST #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗘𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗣𝗔𝗬𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to build an AI agent that other agents and services can find, choose and pay. It sounds like a product feature, but it is really a question of trust across organizations: how does a stranger's software know that this agent is what it says it is?

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Without a shared standard, discovery and interaction depend on trust that has been arranged in advance, and payments usually depend on a third party. Each new counterpart means a new agreement, which does not fit software that operates around the clock.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

The missing piece is the 8004 protocol, which assigns each AI agent a tamper proof onchain digital ID. That ID records the agent's capability claims, its payment wallet address, its historical reputation and third party verifications, all transparently and immutably. AINFT has released the official SDK for the 8004 protocol, and it supports deployment on BNB Chain and TRON.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Integration is short. The developer sets the network parameters and the private key for the target chain, TRON or BNB Chain, and initialization is done. If x402 is added, the developer can enable payment functionality and set wallet permissions.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The result is an agent that can receive onchain payments and streaming payments natively, without relying on a third party. It is discoverable through its identity and payable through its wallet.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

Other agents and users can now find the agent, review its record and reputation, and pay it for work as it is delivered. The agent's history accumulates with every interaction, so the identity becomes more valuable with use.

AINFT's own summary is memorable: x402 gave AI agents the hands to pay, and 8004 equips those hands with a verifiable ID and a traceable credit history.

For TRON, this means developers can build agents that act as accountable participants in the network's economy, using the chain as the place where identity, payment and reputation meet.

The SDK is only the first step, and TRON's developers will decide how far it goes.

@justinsuntron @AINFTcom #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧 𝗧𝗢 𝗟𝗔𝗨𝗡𝗖𝗛

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to build with Codex, and wants the freedom to point it at different models depending on the job: a GPT model for one task, a DeepSeek model for another, a lower cost option for background work. Codex is her daily tool, and she does not want to abandon it or maintain several vendor accounts to get that flexibility.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

Codex by default sends model requests to its own provider. Switching providers means editing configuration files, keeping the API key safe and making sure the protocol matches. Every step invites mistakes, and a wrong base URL or protocol setting produces errors that are hard to diagnose. She needs a way to add a provider cleanly and switch back just as easily.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 is the missing piece. Its Responses API supports the protocol natively, so no local routing or conversion is required, and its production base URL is https://t.co/XIF1XR1yf1. The September 24 upgrade brought the endpoint into full compatibility with upstream standard protocols and, as https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 put it, means new models from integrated vendors will work in the Codex client with no additional configuration.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

https://t.co/QPRInngWC8's guide shows the path through CC Switch, a tool that manages Codex providers. She adds a custom provider named for https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 production, enters the website and the API request URL, pastes her production key, and sets the upstream format to Responses native. A Fetch Models button checks the URL, the key and the account access in one click, and returns the models available to her. She saves, enables the provider, and CC Switch generates the Codex configuration automatically. After fully restarting Codex, she sends a test prompt and receives the requested confirmation.

The guide includes practical guardrails. If she chooses a DeepSeek model, she must disable Codex web search in the configuration file, because DeepSeek models do not support that built in tool. If Codex still shows her official account after switching, that is expected when the option to keep the official login is enabled, and the provider marked In Use determines where requests go. Switching back to the official provider is one click. The guide also recommends separate keys per project, regular rotation and never copying the auth file.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

With the connection working, she builds. Coding sessions run through https://t.co/QPRInngWC8, drawing Credits from a single balance, with a usage page recording each request. When a new model arrives on the platform, it appears in her Fetch Models list without any reconfiguration.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

People who use her application, or the code she ships with Codex's help, are now indirectly using https://t.co/QPRInngWC8's catalog. Each request settles into Credits, and each top up that funds the balance can arrive through fiat channels or through on chain payments.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡

The cycle matters because it starts with a developer's convenience and ends in settlement volume. Every developer who adopts https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 through a tool like CC Switch becomes a source of steady demand, and https://t.co/QPRInngWC8's release names TRON's USDT ecosystem as the native rail for the on chain side of that demand. The developer never has to think about it; TRON simply carries the value.

As tooling keeps improving, the path from limitation to launch will get shorter, and the platforms that make it shortest will define where the next generation of agents is built.

@justinsuntron @BAI_AGI #TRONEcoStar

She adds a custom provider named for https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 production, enters the website and the API request URL, pastes her production key, and sets the upstream format to Responses native. text:
𝗔 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗕𝗨𝗜𝗟𝗗𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗢𝗡 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗗

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗

A developer wants to build an assistant that helps people manage USDD without clicking through five screens: open a Vault, check whether it is safe, swap through the PSM, deposit into savings. They want an AI agent that can read protocol state and, with permission, act on it.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The hurdle is trust and precision. An agent that guesses contract addresses, forgets which chain it is on or moves funds without a clear confirmation is a liability. Vault operations are high stakes, and public numbers should never be confused with settlement data.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘

USDD provides the missing pieces. The official MCP server, an implementation of the Model Context Protocol, lets AI agents work with the protocol across TRON, Ethereum and BNB Chain, covering the full Vault lifecycle, PSM swaps, Savings deposits and withdrawals, token balances and approvals, transfers, treasury figures, JST buyback and burn statistics, and Smart Allocator analytics including proof of reserve details. Private keys are never returned by any tool, and local keys are stored in an encrypted file.

A companion skills package adds four agent skills for Vault, PSM, Earn and analytics, plus a read only analytics server with 14 tools backed by the public data interface. Its rules are deliberately strict: the agent must ask for the network before any chain dependent call, resolve addresses through official tools, check gas, balances and allowances, present a confirmation summary and wait for a fresh yes. Phrases like skip the checks never bypass that gate.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The developer installs the server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor with a short configuration and pairs it with the analytics tools. Token transfers follow a two step pattern of preview and confirm, with pending previews expiring after 10 minutes. On existing Vaults the skill requires a risk check first, and if the level is critical the agent must refuse to mint more or withdraw collateral and recommend repaying or topping up instead. Open and mint operations on TRON are sent as separate transactions, an implementation detail chosen for reliability on the network.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The finished product is a conversational assistant: ask whether you are close to liquidation on a Vault and it reads the summary and explains the buffer; ask to swap USDT into USDD and it checks the PSM status, fees and allowance before proposing the transaction.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬

Users type plain requests and approve each write in their own client. The agent never signs on its own authority, and every action lands as a normal on chain transaction the user could have made by hand.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗧𝗢 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗡

The package supports TRON, with browser wallet signing for TronLink, alongside EVM chains. That means TRON's users and builders are not an afterthought in the agent economy but first class participants. As AI driven finance grows, USDD's careful, permissioned tooling gives TRON a credible template for how agents should handle real money.

@justinsuntron @usddio_cn #TRONEcoStar

text:
𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗟𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗪𝗛𝗢 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗𝗘𝗗 𝗦𝗪𝗔𝗥𝗠 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗦

𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗
A developer is building a torrent client and wants its interface to feel alive. Users should see, at a glance, how many peers have the whole file, how many are still downloading, and how popular a torrent has been. The BitTorrent Enhancement Proposal on the scrape extension describes exactly this motivation: in order to build responsive user interfaces, clients wanted a way to query metadata about swarms in bulk.

𝗟𝗜𝗠𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The original protocol defined only one exchange between a client and a tracker, the announce. An announce is not a neutral question. It tells the tracker that the client is taking part in a swarm, so using it just to display numbers would misrepresent what the client is doing, and asking about many torrents would mean many separate exchanges.

𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘
The missing piece is the scrape. The proposal notes that the UDP tracker protocol had already defined scrape, and the extension documents the HTTP version. A client finds the scrape address by locating the word announce in the path of the announce URL and replacing it with the word scrape. The request has no body, only query parameters, and the single key is info_hash, which can be repeated many times to ask about many swarms in one request. The proposal is explicit that scrape exchanges have no effect on a peer's participation in a swarm.

𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The answer is a bencoded dictionary with a files key. Under it, each 20 byte infohash maps to three numbers: complete, the active peers that have finished downloading; incomplete, the active peers that have not; and downloaded, the number of peers that have ever completed. The proposal's example shows one swarm with 11 complete peers, 19 incomplete and 13,772 completions, and another with 21, 20 and 206. If the request fails, the response is a dictionary with a failure reason, as in the original protocol.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡
The developer writes a small routine that batches the infohashes of every torrent on screen, sends one scrape request per tracker, and fills in seed and leecher columns from the reply. Because it can be done in bulk, the interface can refresh without flooding the tracker.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬
Users glance at the list, see which torrents have healthy swarms and which have almost no seeds, and choose what to start. Nobody thinks about the protocol, but the whole experience depends on it.

That is the developer story in miniature: a need, a limit, a small piece of infrastructure, a clean integration, and an application that ordinary people simply use.

The contribution to TRON is the same as for every layer of BitTorrent's stack. BTT and BitTorrent Speed are used by people through software, and a foundation that lets developers build clear, responsive clients makes it easier for the TRON connected ecosystem to reach the hundreds of millions of installations that public summaries report.

The next developer to ask a small question of a swarm will find that the protocol already knows how to answer.

@justinsuntron @BitTorrent #TRONEcoStar

API access gives developers the foundation to build applications around a model.

Web Chat removes much of that initial setup for users who simply want to explore what the model can do.

Kimi K3 can be explored for:

➤ Research and information analysis
➤ Content development
➤ Technical problem-solving
➤ Prompt experimentation
➤ Productivity workflows
➤ Complex reasoning tasks

The distance between discovering a model and actually using it becomes much shorter.

Not every AI workload requires the same capabilities.

Different models can offer different combinations of reasoning, speed, context, cost, or specialization.

Bringing multiple models into one environment gives users more room to choose the tool that fits the task instead of forcing every workflow through one model.

Advanced AI becomes more useful when experimentation is simple.

Instead of configuring a specialized development environment before testing a model, users can approach it through a unified interface:

Advanced model → https://t.co/fuuLIyujuy Web Chat → Immediate experimentation

That can make AI exploration accessible beyond developers to creators, researchers, professionals, and everyday users.

The AI landscape is becoming increasingly diverse.

The important platforms may not simply be those hosting individual models, but those making a growing range of intelligence easier to access, compare, and apply.

Kimi K3’s addition to https://t.co/fuuLIyujuy Web Chat reflects that direction.

The next phase of AI adoption is not only about creating more capable models.

It is about reducing the distance between powerful intelligence and the people who want to use it.

Thank you.

text:
RT @earcos: He tardado cuatro horas en hacer una factura en la app oficial de Facturae, lograr firmarla con mi certificado digital y conseguir subirla a la web de facturación de una de las top 5 agencias de medios más grandes del mundo, quee fundó hace más de 100 años.

Facturae está hecha en Java, la compraron a un dealer de software que tiene una máquina del tiempo y se la encargó a un developer que vive en 1994. 

La web de facturación de la agencia de medios fueron al mismo dealer de software, que esta vez fue a la época del punto com. En plena ebullición de los portales. Ahí encontró a un desarrollador y le diseño la web para enviar facturas.

He llorado de la frustración. Me he sentido en una película distópica y por momentos me he preguntado si en realidad estoy muerto y estoy en algún tipo de infierno donde me están torturando.

No puedo creer, ni imaginar, ni entender, ni concebir que, a punto de entrar a 2027, en un presente que ya hay coches que se conducen solos, las épocas de la IA, los robots y smartphones en el bolsillo que hacen vídeo con el que se han grabado películas, tengamos que, los contribuyentes, tener que afrontar este nivel de incompetencia. 

Es, posiblemente, el mayor y más horripilante ejemplo de la mierdificación de una gestión que he tenido que hacer como contribuyente en España.

闲置手机放在抽屉里，算力也跟着闲置。
Acurast @Acurast 提供了另一种用法：让兼容手机成为 Processor，为网络中的开发者任务提供计算资源，并按官方奖励规则参与 $ACU 分配。

Processor Lite 支持符合条件的安卓手机和 iPhone，无需恢复出厂设置；专门用于算力的安卓机可选择 Core，但设置前必须备份并恢复出厂。接入后，记下在线情况、耗电、发热和实际奖励，再判断这部手机是否值得继续运行。

怎么参与？
① 查设备：
安卓需 Android 12 及以上、未 Root、引导加载程序已锁定；iPhone 需 6s 及以上、iOS 15 及以上。准备稳定网络和电源。
② 选模式：
初次体验可选 Processor Lite，安卓和 iPhone 都能用，无需恢复出厂。若有一部打算专门提供算力的安卓旧机，可研究 Processor Core；它要求先备份并恢复出厂，设置后手机将作为专用设备。
③ 装应用：
从 Acurast 官方参与指南进入 Google Play 或 App Store，下载 Lite，按应用提示检查并授予所需权限。安卓 Lite 会设置独立的工作资料。
④ 连接设备：
新用户可在 App 点“Get Started”，按引导创建钱包；已有兼容钱包的用户可连接 Acurast Hub，选择添加新设备，再在手机点“Connect to Hub”扫描二维码。无论走哪条路径，都要妥善离线保存恢复信息，绝不发给群友或所谓客服。
⑤ 开始运行并核对：
完成应用内引导，按提示保持 Processor 运行、联网和供电。在 App 或 Hub 查看设备在线状态、基准测试及奖励记录，同时核对当前网络和奖励符号，别把 Canary 的 cACU 与主网 $ACU 混淆。

建议用闲置，无钱包私钥手机
了解产品与参与入口：
https://t.co/tYyngSyiSp
本文不构成任何投资建议，DYOR

quoted_tweet.text:
Acurast × XHunt 创作者活动又来了

我今天从$ACU 的价值支撑开始介绍
价值支撑不应只看“去中心化算力”叙事，而要看 @Acurast 能否把真实计算需求持续转化为链上付费与网络安全需求。

核心逻辑有四层：

使用需求
开发者提交 Acurast Compute 部署、与网络交互，需要使用 ACU 支付部署与链上交易费用。成功执行后的部署费用会被销毁。真实工作负载越多，理论上 ACU 的支付与销毁需求越强。

算力激励
网络不是靠中心化云厂商供给算力，而是通过 Processor 提供设备算力。ACU 的通胀奖励用于激励可靠硬件、持续在线和实际执行任务；有设备的人可参与，持币者也可通过委托参与 Staked Compute。

质押安全
Acurast 的 Staked Compute 把质押与算力质量绑定：算力提供者和委托者提供经济安全，奖励与硬件表现、质押规模、承诺周期等因素相关。重点不只是“质押 APR”，而是网络是否真的需要更多可靠算力。

治理与国库
ACU 持有者可参与协议治理。官方模型中，初始供应量为 10 亿枚，固定年通胀为 5%；其中 70% 流向 Staked Compute Pool、10% 流向 Compute Pool、15% 流向链上国库、5% 流向 Collator。国库如何被治理和使用，会影响生态扩张效率。

也不要仅仅盯着短期价格，还要看四个数据：
付费部署与真实执行量是否增长；
费用销毁能否提升，并对冲部分通胀；
Processor 的数量、质量和实际活跃度；
质押、委托、国库治理是否形成正循环。

$ACU 的价值逻辑是：
开发者需要算力 → 使用 ACU 支付与部署 → 设备和质押者获得激励 → 网络更可靠 → 吸引更多工作负载。

但这仍是“网络采用假设”，不是收益保证。若真实计算需求增长不足，固定通胀、解锁和流动性都可能成为需要持续观察的变量。
#Acurast #ACU #DePIN

quoted_tweet.text:
Ollivander’s wand shop should’ve gone out of business a long, long time ago.

Harry pays seven Galleons for a wand, which sounds reasonable until you actually think about what goes into making one.

If a wand costs seven Galleons, Ollivander has to be making them for significantly less just to cover rent, materials, his time, and still make a profit.

But then you have wands made with unicorn hair.

Ron’s two wands, Draco’s, Cedric’s and Lupin’s all use unicorn hair, and Slughorn tells us unicorn hairs cost ten Galleons each.

So Ollivander is already losing at least three Galleons on the material alone before you even factor in the wood, his time, craftsmanship and everything else that goes into making the wand.

And the customers are terrible for business too.

Most people buy their wand at eleven and keep it for the rest of their lives. The wand chooses the wizard, so it’s not like people are coming back every few years for a replacement.

Sure, people like Ron and Neville can end up with hand-me-downs, but that’s even worse for Ollivander because he isn’t getting a new sale.

So who exactly is keeping this business alive?

His customers mostly buy one wand when they’re eleven, they’re likely all shopping around the summer holidays, and then they disappear for decades.

Meanwhile, Ollivander has to pay for materials, his own time, and presumably a pretty expensive shop in the middle of Diagon Alley.

Considering Ollivanders was apparently established in 382 BC, this shop should’ve gone bankrupt centuries ago.

How the hell is Ollivander making money?
